production.note: US model years, from Kelley Blue Book (a database; no Lamborghini or magazine page naming US model years was found). First: KBB's 2020 Huracán lists "2020 Lamborghini Huracan EVO Coupe 2D" at "631 @ 8000 RPM". Last: KBB's 2023 specs list "EVO Coupe 2D", "631 @ 8000 RPM", AWD (kbb-huracan-2023-specs); KBB's 2024 Huracán lists Tecnica, Sterrato, EVO Spyder and STO but no EVO coupe (kbb-huracan-2024). Lamborghini's release is dated 7 January 2019 (lambo-huracan-evo-release). The EVO RWD and EVO Spyder are separate records.

body.note: Two-door coupe ("EVO Coupe 2D"); the open EVO Spyder is sold under its own name.

drivetrain.note: "Electronically controlled all-wheel drive system (Haldex gen. V) with rear mechanical self-locking differential"

transmission.note: "Dual clutch gearbox LDF (Lamborghini Doppia Frizione) with 7 speeds". No manual was offered.

powerHp.note: Quote (Lamborghini press release as reproduced by supercars.net): "The Huracán EVO outputs 640 hp (470 kW) at 8,000 rpm with 600 Nm of torque delivered at 6,500 rpm." The 640 is Lamborghini's metric (CV/PS) figure: 640 x 0.98632 = 631 hp. No separate US SAE rating was found, so powerStandard is DIN PS, as in the LP 610-4 record. Carscoops (carscoops-huracan-evo): "640 PS (631 HP) at 8,000 rpm"; KBB lists 631 hp.

weightLb.note: DRY weight. 1,422 kg x 2.20462 = 3,135 lb (the release itself prints "lb 3.134"). Quote (Lamborghini technical data as reproduced by supercars.net): "DRY WEIGHT | kg 1.422 (lb 3.134)". Carscoops (carscoops-huracan-evo, by Sergiu Tudose): "1,422 kg (3,135 lbs)" dry. Under the guide's weight order this is step 4: no curb weight for the standard car and no optioned-car curb weight was found from Lamborghini or a major magazine (Evo's and Top Gear's EVO pages opened give no weight). No opened page says whether the EVO's dry figure assumes options (Evo said the LP 610-4's identical 1,422 kg did), so weightQualifier is not set. A car with fluids is heavier.
